authorisation: Kyle: Ok let's do it, referring to independent modern-survey replication of the2018–2022fading and partial recovery.
primary_question: Does independent ASAS-SN photometry reproduce the timing and direction of the ZTF2018–2022fading and subsequent partial recovery?
prediction: Within the same ASAS-SN filter and cameras covering the comparison epochs, J0754 is fainter in2022than2018and subsequently brighter by2025, relative to comparison stars, without relying on cross-survey absolute zero points.
weakening_outcomes: No same-filter independent coverage spans the epochs
Trend depends on camera/quality transitions or shared comparison-star offsets
Sufficient independent data show no fading or opposite direction
Blends, censoring, saturation or a few bad measurements account for the signal
baseline: ZTFsame-exposure corrected annual medians previously saved:2018−0.1896075875,2022+0.1192555875,2025−0.020037475; differences+0.308863175and−0.1392930625mag. These set the question, not an independent fit.
design: Inspect and retain native target catalogue and lightcurve products. Do not mix V and g zero points. Retain camera identifiers; estimate camera offsets from actual overlapping times or comparisons, not arbitrary alignments across gaps. Use documented quality flags, finite positive flux/error, and detection/limit distinction; avoid brightness sigma-clipping. Select comparison stars from previous Gaia matched set without choosing by target outcome.
descriptive_contrast: Same-filter annual medians with at least10measurements in each comparison year, preferably matched-calendar-season/night bins and per-camera estimates. Preserve failed cameras and sparse years. For independence, no ZTFphotometry is used in ASAS-SNcalibration.
decision: Claim corroboration of directional fading only if >=2camera streams or a comparison-corrected common-camera stream spans2018/2022, has adequate sampling, and exhibits a contrast whose robust year/night resampling interval excludes zero, with quality/camera sensitivity agreeing. Recovery assessed separately when2025coverage adequate; do not force a combined PASS.
boundaries: Fluxes are linear only where the survey calibrated photometry supports that. Limits remain limits; no nondetection becomes a magnitude. Different passbands may show different amplitudes. A reproduced modern trend does not identify a cause or link it to the1930s event.
